pain_points.statement: Finance is three weeks behind on invoicing due to inconsistent data between systems, tying up substantial working capital.
pain_points.source_excerpt: finance is 3 weeks behind on invoicing because the data never lines up.

pain_points.statement: Manual operational friction forces the company to consider hiring four additional dispatchers next year at substantial cost.
pain_points.source_excerpt: a 30% reduction in dispatch time means we don't need to hire four additional dispatchers next year, which is about $320k in fully-loaded comp.

desired_state.statement: Achieve industry-standard Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) and free up capital stuck in unbilled receivables.
desired_state.source_excerpt: return to five-day DSO from where we are now frees up about $1.4M in working capital that's currently stuck in unbilled receivables.

success_criteria.statement: Eliminate the need for four dispatcher hires ($320k savings) and unlock $1.4M in working capital through streamlined invoicing.
success_criteria.source_excerpt: we don't need to hire four additional dispatchers next year, which is about $320k in fully-loaded comp. And a return to five-day DSO from where we are now frees up about $1.4M in working capital

risks_unknowns.statement: Stakeholders disagree on the total approved budget cap for Phase 1.
risks_unknowns.source_excerpt: Rita, the budget I approved is $300,000. That's the cap. / Rita, that's not what we discussed. We discussed a six-month Phase 1 in the $250 to $400 range
risks_unknowns.contradiction_note: Rita insists on a strict $300k total budget cap for Phase 1, whereas Sarah recalled an approved budget range between $250k and $400k.

risks_unknowns.statement: Past consulting and internal software project failures have created executive skepticism regarding vendor promises and project delivery.
risks_unknowns.source_excerpt: I have been burned by this exact conversation before. / We've tried internal projects to fix this exact thing twice and they both failed.

pain_points.statement: The core dispatch platform (Routemaster) suffers from severe technical debt and a fragile codebase that severely delays new feature development.
pain_points.source_excerpt: Technical debt in Routemaster. We can't ship features anymore because the codebase is too fragile. Every change takes three times as long as it should.

pain_points.statement: The organization lacks a formal data warehouse, relying on manual Excel exports from Salesforce for business intelligence.
pain_points.source_excerpt: Data warehouse: None (BI is run out of Excel exports from Salesforce)

desired_state.statement: Stakeholders disagree on whether to build integration layers over the legacy system or fully replace it with a commercial SaaS platform.
desired_state.source_excerpt: Sarah thinks this is a workflow problem. I think this is a platform problem. Routemaster is seven years old... and it's at the end of its useful life.
desired_state.contradiction_note: Marcus advocates replacing Routemaster with an external SaaS platform costing $600k in year one, whereas Sarah advocates for targeted, incremental workflow fixes on top of Routemaster within current budget constraints.

success_criteria.statement: Architecture designed during Phase 1 must be modular enough that 60-70% of the workflow logic is preserved if Routemaster is replaced later.
success_criteria.source_excerpt: I'd estimate 60-70% of the Phase 1 work survives a platform change.

risks_unknowns.statement: Integration details with the custom Rails backend and Salesforce CRM are unverified, and technical access is required to assess scope.
risks_unknowns.source_excerpt: Read access to Routemaster — at least the schema and a representative slice of the data.

pain_points.statement: Dispatchers waste significant time manually entering data back and forth between Routemaster and Salesforce.
pain_points.source_excerpt: Too much manual entry between our custom dispatch tool and Salesforce

pain_points.statement: Contracted drivers dislike using the legacy mobile app, causing operational friction and poor user adoption.

desired_state.statement: Streamline dispatcher operations to reduce handling time per load and eliminate redundant double-entry.
desired_state.source_excerpt: Sarah and I talked about a 30% reduction in dispatch time per load

success_criteria.statement: Achieve a 30% reduction in dispatch time per load.
success_criteria.source_excerpt: 30% reduction in dispatch time per load

success_criteria.statement: Stakeholders disagree on the target deployment deadline for the pilot.
success_criteria.source_excerpt: Pilot in production by end of Q3 (Sept 30). / Q3 was your commitment, not mine. I never agreed to Q3. I think Q4 is more realistic if we're doing it right.
success_criteria.contradiction_note: Rita and Sarah insist on an end-of-Q3 pilot launch to prevent funding reallocation, while Marcus asserts Q3 is unrealistic and argues for Q4.

risks_unknowns.statement: Incomplete technical integration from two 2024 company acquisitions presents unknown operational complexity.
risks_unknowns.source_excerpt: Northwind grew 40% in 2024 by acquiring two smaller brokerages. Tech integration from those acquisitions is incomplete.

pain_points.statement: Executive stakeholders lack internal alignment regarding the primary problem and long-term technology trajectory.
pain_points.source_excerpt: Sarah and I have been having a parallel conversation about this for months and we don't agree on what the problem is.

desired_state.statement: Establish a fixed-fee consulting engagement with milestone-based payouts aligned to verifiable business outcomes.
desired_state.source_excerpt: I'll give you a fixed-fee proposal with milestone payments tied to specific outcomes, and if we miss the milestones you don't pay for them.

success_criteria.statement: Secure approval from CFO, CTO, and VP of Operations on a single fixed-fee proposal for Phase 1.
success_criteria.source_excerpt: I want a number in the proposal. Not a range. A number. / Understood. I'll commit to a number.

risks_unknowns.statement: An impending federal ELD compliance mandate in November poses a risk to operating authority if driver app work and compliance dependencies are not properly aligned.
risks_unknowns.source_excerpt: The ELD compliance deadline in November is real. The federal mandate update changes how we have to log driver hours and report them. / Fines, possibly losing our operating authority in some states.
